monitoring-bot: ALERT: pool-gamma-03 throughput down ~45% over the last 5m, worker_restart_count spiked to 18 in last 10m. p99 latency up. see graph: https://grafana/redwood/pool-gamma
Dana L: saw the alert, swapping to incident channel. I'm paged. looking at logs now
Chris R: opening runtime debug session. any recent kernel rollouts to pool-gamma?
Ben S: we pushed a small batching heuristic tweak this morning (optimize small-batch window). Not a kernel change.
Alice M: infra metrics show GPU mem fragmentation rising on node gpu-gamma-03b, frequent cudaAlloc failures across processes
Evan P: running perf profile, but preliminary flame shows lots of time in kv_cache::evict_scan and allocator hot loop
Dana L: kubectl logs for one of the restarting workers: ```
I0523 14:02:12.345678 1 worker.cc:231] launching worker
E0523 14:02:16.122345 1 runtime.cc:98] GPU OOM: failed alloc 2147483648 bytes
E0523 14:02:16.122456 1 runtime.cc:102] Stack: allocator::try_alloc -> kv_cache::alloc_entry -> kv_cache::evict_scan
```
Chris R: that stack matches memory churn from a full-hotset scan pushing evictions into a fragmentation spiral. small objects freed and reallocated -> allocator slabs get fragmented
Ben S: could batch window change have increased simultaneous small batches causing hotset growth? we saw concurrent small requests spike earlier
Alice M: kernel selection logs show multiple fallbacks from fast-int8 to generic-fp16 on the same time window, likely due to memory constraints triggering kernel rejection
Julian (oncall): I'm going to cordon gpu-gamma-03b and move traffic. need a quick mitigation before this spreads
Dana L: agreed. plan: 1) drain pool-gamma-03 nodes 2) temporarily revert small-batch tweak via feature flag 3) remap heavy customers to pool-delta 4) collect full perf traces
Evan P: I'll snapshot the /tmp/prof and capture nvprof traces before restart. also enable kv-cache debug counts (evict_count, scan_len)
Chris R: also note kernel_selector logs: ```
[14:01:55] kernel_selector: prefer_fast_int8 candidate rejected: insufficient_contiguous_free=0x0
[14:01:55] kernel_selector: falling back to generic_fp16
```
Ben S: if fast kernels get rejected we pay more memory and execution time and create more pressure -> feedback loop. looks like noisy-tenant amplified this when a client ramped up small chat completions
Dana L: did we have any rolling restarts or model reloads in the window? deploy-bot?
monitoring-bot: deploy: batch-heuristic-v2 rolled at 2026-05-23T13:51:03Z to pool-gamma (1/3 nodes)
Dana L: ok that aligns. revert queued
Alice M: implementing node drain now, will shift 40% capacity away from gamma. adding temp quota throttle on the noisy API key id: cust-9281
Julian (oncall): opening incident ticket INC-2439, tagging runtime/infra/ml-eng. collecting timestamps and traces there
Evan P: quick mitigation suggestion: raise kv-cache prefetch_threshold to 64 -> reduces aggressive scanning, and bump allocator reclaim window. Doing small test on pool-delta in 2m
Chris R: agree. also add a quick metric to detect kernel fallback rate (>5% fallback per minute) and auto-failover to lower-concurrency routing
Ben S: after revert I'll roll the heuristic to 0% in pool-gamma as hotfix. worth an AB test on delta to confirm behavior
Dana L: timeline: 14:03 drain start, 14:06 revert flag, 14:08 throttle applied, 14:10 first node offlined. monitoring-bot will update on recovered throughput
monitoring-bot: RECOVERY: pool-gamma throughput back to -6% of baseline at 14:18, worker restarts down to 2 in last 10m, p99 slowly returning
Dana L: keeping incident open until 2h post-recovery. logging followups: run allocator splay, increase slab compaction frequency, and add kernel-selector circuit breaker to avoid repeated fallbacks
Chris R: I'll file a perf regression PR with traces and kernel-selection traces + propose a guard in selector: if fallback_rate > threshold, reduce concurrency for that pool
Ben S: capture failing request ids for eval later. looks like a specific workload pattern (many short seqs) triggered the hotset
Alice M: good job folks. postmortem template assigned to me, will include mitigation plan: better hotset isolation, kv-cache eviction heuristics, and emergency rollback path for batching heuristics
Dana L: thanks. closing temporary escalation but leaving incident open for analysis. :thumbsup:
